 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.11.2018 passed by Ist MACT, Manawar, district Dhar in Claim Case No.45/2017 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
Ganesh vs Purushottam on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150710011/
1 for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,34,987/- along with interest.

entities.text: Ganesh vs Purushottam on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT

Permanent disability -Rs.210600/-
 (Rs.5000 x 12 x 13 x 27/100 PD)

Medical expenses -Rs.4,87,387/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.25,000/-

Mental suffering -Rs.4,000/-
 Special diet -Rs.2,000/-

Attendant charges/transportation -Rs.1,000/-
 Loss of wages -Rs.5,000/-

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Perusal of the impugned award it is found that the Tribunal has not awarded any sum under the head of future prospects in the light of the judgment of the apex court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as permanent disability is concerned, it is found that the appellant/claimant suffered fracture of 5th metacarpal bone of right hand, femur and tibia fibula of leg and fracture of radius ulna right hand and dislocation.
He suffered 44% disability of tibia fibula, 22% of femur bone and 20% of radius ulna.

The Tribunal has assessed 27% permanent disability for the whole body,
which in the considered opinion of this Court in on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced to 40%.
The compensation awarded under other conventional heads is also on the lower side.

In view of the above, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be recalculated as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Permanent disability -Rs.3,90,000/-
(i.e. Rs.5000 25% FP x 12 x 13 (multiplier) x 40/100 PD) Medical expenses -Rs.4,87,387/-

Mental suffering -Rs.4,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.25,000/-

Ganesh vs Purushottam on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150710011/
2  Special diet -Rs.5000/-
Attendant charges/transportation -Rs.10,000/- Loss of income during treatment -Rs.5,000/-
-------------------
TOTAL Rs.9,26,387/-
7. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.9,26,387/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.7,34,987/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,91,400/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,91,400/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
